headline: Michigan cannabis excise tax beat alcohol taxes by 68% in FY 2025-26
dek: Michigan collected $287.2 million in cannabis excise tax against $171.4 million from alcohol; Colorado has sent $703.5 million to school building.
key_points: Michigan's 10% adult-use cannabis excise tax raised $287.2 million in fiscal year 2025-26, about 68% more than beer, wine and liquor excise taxes combined, per House Fiscal Agency figures.
Cannabis excise revenue still fell 6.1% from $305.7 million a year earlier; alcohol excise revenue fell about 9.3%.
The figure excludes Michigan's separate 24% wholesale cannabis tax, which began on 1 January 2026.
Colorado has directed $703.5 million of $851.9 million in cannabis excise tax to school construction since 2014, a legislative staff briefing shows.
body: Two state budget documents published this month put numbers on what legal cannabis is worth to state treasuries, and on how that value is starting to shrink. In Michigan, the adult-use excise tax out-earned every alcohol excise tax combined for a second year. In Colorado, the oldest adult-use market, cumulative cannabis excise revenue for school buildings passed $700 million.

Both sets of figures were reported by The Marijuana Herald on 19 November from state documents: a monthly revenue update from the Michigan House Fiscal Agency dated 17 November, and a 12 November briefing by staff of Colorado's Joint Budget Committee. We checked the alcohol figures against the Michigan report itself; we could not open the Colorado briefing and rely on the Herald's account of it.
## Michigan: cannabis ahead of beer, wine and liquor

Michigan collected $287.2 million from its recreational cannabis excise tax in fiscal year 2025-26, according to the Herald's reading of the House Fiscal Agency report. Beer and wine taxes brought in $41.1 million and the liquor excise tax $130.3 million, $171.4 million together. Cannabis was ahead by about $115.8 million, or roughly 68%.

The gap widened from the year before, when cannabis raised $305.7 million against $189 million from alcohol, a lead of about 62%. But it widened because alcohol fell faster, not because cannabis grew. Cannabis excise revenue dropped 6.1%. Liquor excise revenue fell 10.8%, from $146.1 million, and beer and wine revenue fell 4%, from $42.9 million. Combined alcohol excise revenue was down about 9.3%, on our calculation.
## What the Michigan figure leaves out

The comparison needs three cautions. First, it covers only the 10% excise tax that adult-use buyers pay on top of Michigan's 6% sales tax. General sales tax on either cannabis or alcohol is not counted, so this is not a measure of total tax from each industry.

Second, it does not include the 24% wholesale cannabis tax Michigan introduced on 1 January 2026. That tax is separate from the excise tax in the fiscal agency's line and is not in the $287.2 million, the Herald noted. The state's total take from cannabis in the fiscal year is therefore higher than the headline figure.

Third, the excise tax is a percentage of the retail price, so it tracks spending, not volume. A 6.1% fall in excise revenue means shoppers spent about 6.1% less at the till; it does not by itself show they bought less cannabis. The report does not say how much of the fall is price and how much is volume, and neither do we.
> Michigan's cannabis tax is winning a race against alcohol in which both runners are slowing down.
## Colorado: $703.5 million for school buildings

Colorado collected about $851.9 million in cannabis excise tax from fiscal year 2013-14 through 2025-26, and $703.5 million of that went to the Public School Capital Construction Assistance Fund, according to the Herald's account of the Joint Budget Committee staff briefing. That is about 83% of all excise revenue, on our calculation. The fund pays for the Building Excellent Schools Today programme, which gives competitive grants to districts and charter schools to build, replace and repair school buildings.

The link is written into the state constitution. Amendment 64, which voters approved in 2012, sends the first $40 million of excise tax each year to school construction. Lawmakers have since changed how revenue above that amount is shared. Of the remainder, about $67.6 million went to the Public School Permanent Fund and $80.8 million was moved to the State Public School Fund in fiscal year 2020-21.

For fiscal year 2025-26 alone, about $58.4 million of cannabis tax went to K-12 education funds: $38.9 million from the wholesale excise tax and $19.5 million from the special retail sales tax. Colorado's three cannabis taxes together raised about $219.6 million in the year, so schools received roughly 27 cents of each cannabis tax dollar. Colorado charges a 15% excise tax on certain wholesale transfers and a separate 15% special sales tax on adult-use purchases.
## A shrinking base

The Herald notes that Colorado's annual excise collections have fallen from their 2021 peak. One figure in the briefing shows what that means: the wholesale excise tax sent $38.9 million to education in 2025-26, just under the $40 million a year that Amendment 64 earmarks first for school construction. When collections sit near or below that line, there is little or nothing left over from the excise tax for other uses. That is our reading of the published totals, not a statement from the committee's staff.

Michigan is earlier on the same curve. Revenue is still large but fell in the latest year, and the state added a wholesale tax in 2026 on top of the excise tax. MJBizDaily reported on 5 November that Michigan's cannabis industry hopes the change in control of the legislature will bring a repeal of that tax. The fiscal agency's figures give both sides an argument: cannabis is one of the state's most productive excise taxes, and its base is already contracting.
## What it means

For operators, these documents matter because they shape how legislators see the industry at budget time. A tax that out-earns alcohol is hard to cut. A tax whose revenue is falling invites either a higher rate, which Michigan has already tried at wholesale level, or relief to protect the base, which California chose in 2025. For investors, the direction of state revenue is a useful cross-check on reported sales: in both states, the tax data points to flat or falling spending in mature markets.
## What to watch

Watch Michigan's 2027 legislative session for bills on the 24% wholesale tax. The House Fiscal Agency publishes revenue updates monthly, which will show whether the excise decline continues into fiscal year 2026-27. In Colorado, the Joint Budget Committee is working through briefings for the 2027-28 budget, where the split of cannabis revenue between school construction and other programmes is set.
